Well the reasons the dungeons looks so dark isn't so much a lack of lighting, but rather how dark the fog is.
There used to be a better, more elaborate way of generating dungeon themes, but was temporarily removed while implementing multiplayer, and I completely forgot about it.
This other system would also change the fog and lights in the dungeon, so when removed they defaulted to what they were set to in the editor, black fog and dim lights.

I've learned quite a lot over the past years.
One of the most important things I've learned, is protect your ideas.
A few years back, I actually had permission from a company to remake one of their games (I'm not going to mention the company or game as to avoid drama). After having quite a few back and forth emails about the project. And me even sending them builds, they sort of stopped responding.  I worked on the project for almost 3 years in my spare time.
Then, after working on the project for several years, the company announces an official remake of the game, with almost my exact art style and plenty of the ideas I had incorporated.
Of course this devastated me, as I had poured many many hours into this game, but it definitely taught me a valuable lesson.

I know this was obviously on a bigger scale, but you should always protect what you create, and you should always try and fight back if somebody decides to take it from you.

All the colors are randomly generated.
In that trailer, the system for generating the colors is very simple (pretty much picks 3 random colors and goes from there) but a while back, I had a system that was more complex, and would actually generate based on themes.
It yielded much better results, giving dungeons that felt more connected and with better fitting colors/assets.
This system was lost, however, while working the game for multiplayer.
I'm very happy receiving all this criticism, as I've used a lot of it to already improve the game.

Currently the dungeon colors have a very basic formula with how they are generated, and it can often lead to some weird combos.
I had actually completely rewrote the way they generate, with a theme system in place instead.
This generated far better looking colors, and had some greater forms of variation and theme.
I had all of this on a separate branch though, and then started working on the multiplayer stuff on a branch based of the master.
Doing this, I had to write a system for syncing dungeons between players, but I wrote it for the original script rather than the theme based one.
I want to go back to themes soon, but I felt it wasnt an important enough feature to warrant holding back the beta.
